title: Dynamic tenant RPS contracts and isolation proxy
creator: Priya Nair
description: Introduce an "isolation proxy" and runtime RPS contract layer to guarantee per-tenant throughput for Dedicated customers while protecting the GPU fleet from noisy neighbors. This ticket implements: 1) a lightweight sidecar/proxy that enforces tenant RPS contracts (steady and burst windows), 2) integration with autoscaling and token-bucket burst credits, and 3) a soft-preemption policy to gracefully shed excess load with informative client errors and automatic fallback to lower-cost model variants.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant steady RPS and burst window enforced by isolation proxy with configurable contract parameters in tenant config
Autoscaler honors RPS signals and can scale up dedicated lanes within release latency targets
Under sustained overload, the system returns 429 with Retry-After and increments tenant quota-metrics; documented fallback to best-effort model branch occurs
Telemetry produced: tenant_rps, tenant_token_fill, tenant_burst_remaining, preemption_count, migration_events; dashboards created in Console
Performance: p95 latency for routed requests <= 250ms at contracted throughput for 95% of tenants in canary cluster
E2E load tests (k6) reproduce expected behavior for steady and burst traffic patterns and pass in CI
technical_design: Isolation proxy runs as an Envoy-like sidecar in Dedicated lanes; small binary (~6MB) implemented in Rust for low overhead
Per-tenant token bucket with two windows: steady (1s) and burst (60s). Buckets persist in local in-memory store with Redis fallback for cross-node tenancy migration
Proxy exposes short-circuit API to serving runtime to signal preemption (soft) or hard-block for immediate enforcement
Autoscaler listens to aggregate tenant_rps and token_fill signals. For tenants with binding SLA, autoscaler can provision pre-warmed lane capacity via reserved GPU pools
Lease manager supports moving tenant routing in-band: isolation proxy can mark tenant as 'migrating' and proxy-level buffering will be enabled until destination lane accepts traffic
Fallback policy: when a tenant exhausts burst credits, proxy first attempts graceful downgrade (model_variant=cost-optimized), then returns 429 if downgrade unavailable
Security: proxy authenticates with control-plane using mTLS and tenant ACL tokens; audit events emitted for quota violations
implementation_notes: Step 1: isolation proxy library + small binary. Keep public API minimal: Allow(request), Observe(success|failure), InspectQuota(tenant_id)
Step 2: Instrument runtime to emit per-request tenant_id and latency tags for Console dashboards
Step 3: Autoscaler hook that consumes token_bucket_saturation and issues scale requests to allocator service
Step 4: Add migration orchestrator that coordinates route change with graceful handoff and retention of KV cache pointers
Prefer Redis Streams as cross-node signal bus; ensure 95th-percentile write+read latency < 5ms under load
test_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket edge cases (concurrent drains, refill races)
Integration tests with mock allocator: simulate reserve/scale-up/scale-down cycles
k6-based load scenarios: steady at contract, spike burst, multi-tenant noisy neighbor stress test (one tenant blasts 10x RPS)
Chaos test: kill proxy instance during migration to validate buffering and retry semantics
Performance benchmark: cold-start overhead of proxy < 8ms and per-request CPU overhead < 0.25ms on p4d instance
rollout_plan: Phase A - dev cluster: run proxy behind feature flag for internal tenants (1 week)
Phase B - canary: enable for 10 dedicated customers with simple contracts (2 weeks), monitor telemetry and SLOs
Phase C - staged rollout: 25% of Dedicated lanes, refine autoscaler thresholds and token bucket params
Phase D - GA: full config rollout with customer opt-in and admin Console UI to edit RPS contracts
Kill-switch: control-plane flag to bypass proxy and revert to legacy routing within 15s
risks: State synchronization: race conditions when migrating tenant state between nodes could cause transient under-counting or double-charge of burst credits
Latency overhead: adding proxy hop may regress tail latencies if not optimized; requires careful benchmarking
Complexity in autoscaler tuning: miscalibrated thresholds could overprovision (cost) or underprovision (SLO violation)
Operator UX: exposing too many contract knobs could confuse customers; provide sensible defaults and guardrails
